name: Processor B (9q, dense K5-minus-2 core + sparse tail)
design_rationale: Co-designed for this problem: the knapsack cost Hamiltonian couples every pair of items (w_i*w_j terms => K5).  Qubits 0-3 form a K4 and qubit 4 couples to 1 and 2, so 8 of the 10 required ZZ pairs are native and only 2 need routing.  Qubits 5-8 form a sparse tail (slack bits of formulation S) so the whole chip keeps 12 edges = the same budget as the heavy-hex reference.  A 20-seed sweep showed it beats the 3x3 grid (bipartite, no triangles) and the heavy-hex reference on SWAPs/CX at p=1 and p=2.
